  In-person /Telephonic / Video Conference Meeting

  MAYOR’S CITYWIDE ELECTRICAL RESILIENCE (MCER)
  AD HOC COMMITTEE MEETING

  AGENDA

  Wednesday, August 30, 2023
  2:00 p.m.

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54953, members of the Beverly Hills Mayor’s Citywide Electrical
  Resilience (MCER) Ad Hoc Committee and staff may participate in this meeting in-person or via a
  teleconference. In the interest of maintaining appropriate social distancing, members of the public can
  participate in the meeting by using the link or phone numbers below.

  Anyone who participates at the meeting and/or enters the City Council Chamber or Commission meeting
  room is subject to having their image and/or voice displayed. These recordings will remain publicly
  accessible in perpetuity.

  How to Submit a Public Comment:
  Audio/oral: 1 669 900 9128 US or 1 833 548 0282 (Toll-Free)
  Email: bhelectricresilience@beverlyhills.org
  Video: https://beverlyhills-org.zoom.us/my/committee
  Meeting ID: 516 191 2424
  Passcode: 90210
  To watch video live: https://www.beverlyhills.org/live
  In-Person: Submit a Speaker Card to the Recording Secretary

  It is recommended that written public comments be submitted to the Mayor’s Citywide Electrical
  Resilience (MCER) Ad Hoc Committee Recording Secretary by 2:00 PM on the meeting date. Public
  comments will also be taken during the meeting when the topic is being reviewed by the Mayor’s
  Citywide Electrical Resilience (MCER) Ad Hoc Committee. Written comments should identify the Agenda
  Item number or topic in the subject line of the email.

  In order to be read at the meeting, written comments will be allowed with a maximum of 350 words,
  which corresponds to approximately three (3) minutes of speaking time. If a comment is received after
  the agenda item is heard, it will not be a part of the record.

  The Committee may act on any item listed on the agenda.

  Recordings of meetings are available online within three business days of the meeting. Visit www.beverlyhills.org to access those
  recordings.
 Mayor’s Electrical Resilience Committee Meeting

  Mayor Gold will lead introduce the Committee purpose and state the City’s innovations to date.

2. COMMITTEE MEMBER INTRODUCTIONS
  Committee members will introduce themselves.

3. WHAT IS THE RESILIENCE PROBLEM
  City Consultant Mariko Geronimo will lead the discussion on the resilience problem.

4. GRID AND MICROGRID FUNDAMENTALS
  City Consultant Mariko Geronimo will lead the discussion on grid and microgrid basics.

5. ELECTRICITY RESILIENCE TERMS & DEFINITIONS
  Staff and Consultant Mariko Geronimo will provide terms and definitions for clarification and discussion and

minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210

  MAYOR'S CITYWIDE ELECTRICAL RESILIENCE (MCER)
  AD HOC COMMITTEE MEETING HIGHLIGHTS
  Wednesday, August 30, 2023
  2:00 PM
MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  August 30, 2023 / 2:00 PM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian A. Gold, M.D., Vice Mayor Lester Friedman,
  Committee Member Jeff Wolfe, Committee Member Mark Nehoray,
  Committee Member Linda Spiegel, Committee Member Ethan
  Bearman, Assistant City Manager Ryan Gohlich, Director of Public
  Works Shana Epstein, Management Analyst Audrey Wright,
  Consultant Mariko Geronimo of Lumen Energy Strategy, LLC
COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Members of the public were allowed to directly address the Committee on any item not
  listed on the agenda.

  Public Speakers: Public comment was heard from David Gingold.

1) MAYOR GOLD INTRODUCES THE COMMITTEE PURPOSE & PROVIDES A RECAP OF
  THE CITY’S ENERGY INNOVATIONS TO DATE
  Mayor Gold introduced the Committee’s purpose and provided a short update on the City’s
  innovations to date, including solar panels on City buildings, the City’s participation in the
  Clean Power Alliance Power Ready Program, completed Energy Efficiency Investments such
  as the replacement of older electrical equipment, the replacement of the streetlight system to
  LED with smart controllers, the City’s participation in a Community Choice Aggregation that
  provides Beverly Hills renewable electricity and the City’s draft Climate Action and Adaptation
  Plan (CAAP) with the goals of making the City resilient from the effects of climate change and
  reducing GHG emissions.

2) COMMITTEE MEMBER INTRODUCTIONS
  Committee Member Bearman, Committee Member Spiegel, Committee Member Nehoray,
  Committee Member Wolfe, Vice Mayor Friedman, Mayor Gold, Assistant City Manager Ryan
  Gohlich, Director of Public Works Shana Epstein, Management Analyst Audrey Wright and
  Consultant Mariko Geronimo introduced themselves and provided a brief summary of their
  background.
   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210

3) WHAT IS THE RESILIENCE PROBLEM
  Consultant Mariko Geronimo introduced the item, provided a short presentation and led the
  discussion. Energy efficiency and Southern California Edison (SCE) system dependence,
  outages and power grid performance were discussed. It was noted that most power outages
  are driven by equipment failure (incorrect equipment load, water in vaults, accidents and/or
  other damage, etc.), system age and unknown causes. Inclement weather and performance
  of system upgrades also lend to outages. A key factor in electricity production is that electricity
  supply must near exactly match the electricity demand in order to properly function. It was
  noted the City of Beverly Hills has a higher rate of failures than SCE’s system average.

4) GRID AND MICROGRID FUNDAMENTALS
  Consultant Mariko Geronimo led the discussion on grid and microgrid basics.

5) ELECTRICITY RESILIENCE TERMS & DEFINITIONS
  This item was provided for informational purposes.

6) CRITERIA FOR DISCERNING THE ELECTRICITY RESILIENCE SOLUTION
  Consultant Mariko Geronimo provided criteria for discerning the electrical resilience solution
  for the City and led the Committee discussion.

7) FUTURE MEETING TOPIC RECOMMENDATIONS
  Committee members discussed future topics of discussion. Defining reasons or patterns for
  outages to customize solutions, undergrounding and the problems associated with it, a
  potential City goal of providing a general survivable level of electrical independence during an
  emergency, critical electrical functions, limited residential electrical functions, a clear
  statement of what the Committee is attempting to provide for in terms of electricity during an
  outage, infrastructure maintenance, SCE oversight, power outage mitigation, working within
  SCE’s construct, determining realistic goals, building resources close to customers,
  pinpointing what electricity is needed for, identifying customers and customer segments,
  reducing power outages, providing electricity alternatives during an emergency, deciphering
  commercial and residential needs and providing a level of home resiliency audits were
  discussed.

8) DIRECTOR’S REPORT
  Director of Public Works Shana Epstein requested Committee members complete the
  Evaluation Criteria Matrix and return to staff, to send future meeting topics to staff, as well as
  asked if the Committee prefers to schedule a recurring meeting the last Wednesday of every
  month. The Committee decided upon monthly meetings from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m., the last
  Wednesday of each month, depending upon schedules.

ADJOURNMENT
  Date / Time:  August 30, 2023/ 3:41 PM
